page: Microsoft Azure L1ps_v5 is an entry-level virtual machine within the storage-optimized Lpsv5 family, built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance allocates a single dedicated ARM64 vCPU paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a generous 1:8 core-to-memory ratio. Discrete GPU acceleration is absent, maintaining a resource profile oriented around energy-efficient compute, memory capacity, and local disk performance.

A primary hardware feature is the integrated local storage, consisting of a 241 GB NVMe SSD that delivers low-latency host-attached disk access for scratch space, temporary indexing, and caching. The platform also provides support for Azure Premium Storage for applications requiring durable persistent block volumes. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included with the virtual machine.

With its compact single-core allocation and bundled NVMe capacity, the instance offers cost-efficient access to high-speed local disk without the overhead of larger multi-core footprints. The single vCPU introduces a clear tradeoff, as parallel processing capability is fundamentally constrained. The hardware configuration is best suited for small database servers, Redis caching instances, log aggregation, and ARM-targeted continuous integration tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure L1ps_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a 64-bit ARM processor managed through Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provisions 1 dedicated ARM64 vCPU and 8.0 GB of memory, delivering a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio suited for memory-backed tasks. Storage capabilities are highlighted by an integrated 241 GB local NVMe SSD, ensuring low-latency disk I/O directly attached to the host, alongside compatibility with Premium Storage remote disks. The instance operates without discrete GPU acceleration and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With its single-core footprint, the instance balances dedicated CPU access and fast local ephemeral storage against limited parallel processing throughput. This hardware profile makes the instance particularly effective for lightweight database engines, caching tiers, logging agents, and development environments requiring local NVMe storage on ARM architecture.
